reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) discusses synthesis conditions, atomic mobility, and nanoparticle formation on supports, but none provides data or direct support for surface premelting, melting point depression, or the inward propagation of a liquid shell in FeNiCrCoCu or any HEA nanoparticles. The key premises thus lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Nanoparticle surfaces have lower atomic coordination and higher free energy than the bulk
This surface condition causes a local depression of the melting point relative to the bulk
Surface premelting (formation of a liquid-like shell) occurs below the bulk melting point
The liquid-like shell propagates inward to drive complete melting
Multicomponent (high-entropy) nanoparticles exhibit this premelting behavior more distinctly than lower-entropy or larger particles
